costfun.Description: Define the type of cost function.

sensor_power_photovoltaics.Description: This is the name of the photovoltaic power-produced sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. For example: ‘sensor.power_photovoltaics’.

sensor_power_photovoltaics_forecast.Description: This is the name of the photovoltaic forecast sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. For example: ‘sensor.p_pv_forecast’.

sensor_power_battery.Description: The name of the signed AC-side battery power sensor in Watts from Home Assistant, used by battery self-identification. Either sign convention works (it is auto-detected). Only retrieved when set_use_battery_identification is true. For example: ‘sensor.power_battery’. With number_of_batteries > 1, provide a list of exactly number_of_batteries entity ids, one per battery, index-matched to the battery config lists; a single sensor is never broadcast to more than one battery.

sensor_battery_state_of_charge.Description: The name of the measured battery state of charge sensor in percent from Home Assistant, used by battery self-identification. Only retrieved when set_use_battery_identification is true. For example: ‘sensor.battery_state_of_charge’. With number_of_batteries > 1, provide a list of exactly number_of_batteries entity ids, one per battery, index-matched to the battery config lists; a single sensor is never broadcast to more than one battery.

sensor_power_load_no_var_loads.friendly_name: Sensor power loads with no variable loads
sensor_power_load_no_var_loads.Description: The name of the household power consumption sensor in Watts from Home Assistant. The deferrable loads that we will want to include in the optimization problem should be subtracted from this sensor in HASS. For example: ‘sensor.power_load_no_var_loads’

sensor_replace_zero.friendly_name: Sensor to replace NAN values with 0s
sensor_replace_zero.Description: The list of retrieved variables that we would want to replace NANs (if they exist) with zeros.

sensor_linear_interp.friendly_name: Sensor to replace NAN values with linear interpolation
sensor_linear_interp.Description: The list of retrieved variables that we would want to interpolate NANs values using linear interpolation

ssl_no_verify.Description: Set to true to disable SSL verification when connecting to Home Assistant. Useful if using self-signed certificates (HTTPS with IP address).

use_websocket.friendly_name: Use Home Assistant websocket for data retrieval
use_websocket.Description: Enable Home Assistant websocket as data source instead of Home Assistant API. This allows for longer historical data retention and better performance for machine learning models.

use_influxdb.Description: Enable InfluxDB as data source instead of Home Assistant API. This allows for longer historical data retention and better performance for machine learning models. Only supports version 1.x.

influxdb_host.Description: The IP address or hostname of your InfluxDB instance. Defaults to localhost.

influxdb_port.Description: The port number for your InfluxDB instance. Defaults to 8086.

influxdb_database.Description: The name of the InfluxDB database containing your Home Assistant data. Defaults to 'homeassistant'.

influxdb_measurement.Description: The measurement name where your sensor data is stored. Defaults to 'W' for the Home Assistant integration.

influxdb_retention_policy.Description: The retention policy to use for InfluxDB queries. Defaults to 'autogen'.

influxdb_use_ssl.Description: Enables HTTPS on InfluxDB connections. Defaults to 'false'.

influxdb_verify_ssl.Description: Enables SSL verification of the certificate (e.g. Let's Encrypt) on InfluxDB connections. Defaults to 'false'.

continual_publish.Description: set to True to save entities to .json after an optimization run. Then automatically republish the saved entities (with updated current state value) every freq minutes. entity data saved to data_path/entities.

logging_level.Description: DEBUG provides detailed diagnostic information, INFO gives general operational messages, WARNING highlights potential issues, and ERROR indicates critical problems that may disrupt functionality.

optimization_time_step.Description: The time step to resample retrieved data from hass. This parameter is given in minutes. It should not be defined too low or you will run into memory problems when defining the Linear Programming optimization. Defaults to 30

historic_days_to_retrieve.Description: We will retrieve data from now to days_to_retrieve days. Defaults to 2

load_negative.Description: Set this parameter to True if the retrieved load variable is negative by convention. Defaults to False

set_zero_min.Description: Set this parameter to True to give a special treatment for a minimum value saturation to zero for power consumption data. Values below zero are replaced by nans. Defaults to True.

method_ts_round.Description: Set the method for timestamp rounding, options are: first, last and nearest.

delta_forecast_daily.Description: The number of days for forecasted data; can be overridden at runtime via runtimeparams. Defaults to 1. For naive-mpc, the forecast window is now extended automatically to cover a longer prediction_horizon, so this parameter usually need not be set manually for multi-day MPC runs.

load_forecast_method.Description: The load forecast method that will be used. The options are ‘csv’ to load a CSV file or ‘naive’ for a simple 1-day persistence model.

mlforecaster_weather_features.Description: Optional list of weather covariate columns to feed the 'mlforecaster' load forecast model as exogenous inputs, in addition to the always-present calendar features. Useful when the load is weather-dependent (e.g. a heat pump). Leave empty to disable (default). Supported values: temp_air, relative_humidity, cloud_cover, wind_speed, ghi, direct_radiation, diffuse_radiation, precipitation, heating_degree, cooling_degree. The values are sourced from the Open-Meteo weather forecast; heating_degree/cooling_degree are derived from the temperature. Only used when 'Load forecast method' above is mlforecaster.

set_total_pv_sell.Description: Set this parameter to true to consider that all the PV power produced is injected to the grid. No direct self-consumption. The default is false, for a system with direct self-consumption.

publish_deferrable_load_states.Description: When true, EMHASS additionally publishes one interpretable command sensor per deferrable load (sensor.p_deferrableN_state) whose state is 'on', 'off' or 'variable' for the current timestep, with the full optimized on/off/variable plan as a 'schedule' attribute. This lets automations act on a clear command instead of thresholding the power forecast themselves. Defaults to false.

num_threads.friendly_name: Number of threads to use for the LP solver
num_threads.Description: Set the number of threads for the LP solver to use, when supported by the solver. Defaults to 0 (autodetect)

lp_solver_timeout.Description: Set the maximum time (in seconds) for the LP solver. Defaults to 45.

lp_solver_mip_rel_gap.Description: For mixed-integer problems (with binary variables), the solver stops when the solution is within this percentage of optimal. Valid range: 0 to 1 (0% to 100%). Higher values (e.g., 0.05 = 5%) solve faster with minimal quality loss. Defaults to 0.01 (within 1% of optimal), which keeps deep-horizon problems from timing out without a published plan. Set to 0 for exact optimal.

weather_forecast_method.Description: This will define the weather forecast method that will be used. options are 'open-meteo', 'Solcast', 'solar.forecast' (forecast.solar) and 'csv' to load a CSV file. When loading a CSV file this will be directly considered as the PV power forecast in Watts.

weather_forecast_pv_quantile_bias.Description: Blend factor that biases the Solcast PV forecast toward its conservative P10 (low) estimate. 0 (default) uses the central P50 estimate, i.e. unchanged behaviour. 1 uses the P10 estimate. Intermediate values blend linearly: estimate = bias*P10 + (1-bias)*P50. Higher values produce more defensive plans (more battery reserve held when solar is uncertain). Only effective with weather_forecast_method set to solcast. Defaults to 0.

open_meteo_cache_max_age.Description: The maximum age, in minutes, of the cached open-meteo json response, after which a new version will be fetched from Open-Meteo. Defaults to 30.

maximum_power_from_grid.Description: The maximum power that can be supplied by the utility grid in Watts (consumption). Defaults to 9000.

maximum_power_to_grid.Description: The maximum power that can be supplied to the utility grid in Watts (injection). Defaults to 9000.

inverter_is_hybrid.Description: Set to True to consider that the installation inverter is hybrid for PV and batteries (Default False)

inverter_ac_output_max.friendly_name: Max hybrid inverter AC output power
inverter_ac_output_max.Description: Maximum hybrid inverter output power from combined PV and battery discharge.

inverter_ac_input_max.friendly_name: Max hybrid inverter AC input power
inverter_ac_input_max.Description: Maximum hybrid inverter input power from grid to charge battery.

inverter_efficiency_dc_ac.friendly_name: Hybrid inverter efficency DC to AC
inverter_efficiency_dc_ac.Description: Hybrid inverter efficiency from the DC bus to AC output. (percentage/100)

inverter_efficiency_ac_dc.friendly_name: Hybrid inverter efficency AC to DC
inverter_efficiency_ac_dc.Description: Hybrid inverter efficiency when charging from the AC input to DC bus. (percentage/100)

inverter_stress_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh) applied at the inverter's nominal power to penalise high loads. Currently implemented as a quadratic curve (Cost ∝ Power²), incentivising 'low and slow' operation to reduce thermal stress and smooth power flows.

inverter_stress_segments.Description: The number of linear segments used to approximate the stress cost curve. Higher values increase accuracy but may slightly increase computation time.

compute_curtailment.Description: Set to True to compute a special PV curtailment variable (Default False). When enabled, curtailment that is cost-equivalent is scheduled as late as possible in the optimization horizon

load_cost_forecast_method.Description: Define the method that will be used for load cost forecast. The options are ‘hp_hc_periods’ for peak and non-peak hours contracts, and ‘csv’ to load custom cost from CSV file.

load_peak_hour_periods.Description: A list of peak hour periods for load consumption from the grid. This is useful if you have a contract with peak and non-peak hours.

load_peak_hours_cost.Description: The cost of the electrical energy during peak hours

load_offpeak_hours_cost.Description: The cost of the electrical energy during off-peak hours

production_price_forecast_method.friendly_name: PV power production price forecast method
production_price_forecast_method.Description: Define the method that will be used for PV power production price forecast. This is the price that is paid by the utility for energy injected into the grid. The options are ‘constant’ for a constant fixed value or ‘csv’ to load custom price forecasts from a CSV file.

photovoltaic_production_sell_price.Description: The paid price for energy injected to the grid from excess PV production in currency/kWh.

thermal_gas_price_forecast_method.Description: When the heat pump is hybrid, define the gas price as a constant fixed value or read it from a column in the thermal data CSV.

thermal_gas_price.Description: Fixed gas price in €/kWh used for hybrid heat-pump gas cost calculations.

thermal_gas_price_col.Description: Column name in the thermal data CSV containing the gas price series in €/kWh when gas price method is set to csv.

set_use_pv.Description: Set to True if we should consider an solar PV system. Defaults to False

set_use_adjusted_pv.Description: Set to True if we should consider an adjusted solar PV system. Defaults to False

adjusted_pv_regression_model.Description: Set the type of regression model that will be used to adjust the solar PV production to local conditions. Available models are defined in REGRESSION_METHODS (machine_learning_regressor.py). Defaults to LassoRegression

adjusted_pv_solar_elevation_threshold.Description: This is the solar elevation threshold parameter used to identify the early morning or late evening periods. Defaults to 10.

adjusted_pv_model_max_age.Description: Maximum age in hours before the adjusted PV regression model is re-fitted. If the saved model is older than this value, a new model will be trained using fresh historical data. Set to 0 to force re-fitting on every call. Defaults to 24 hours (1 day).

set_use_battery_identification.Description: Opt-in, default off. When enabled, EMHASS learns the battery usable capacity and round-trip efficiency from Home Assistant history (signed battery power and measured state of charge) instead of relying only on the hand-entered values. It requires set_use_battery to be true and the sensor_power_battery and sensor_battery_state_of_charge sensors. In v1 this is advisory only: it never changes the configured battery values used by the optimizer. Defaults to false.

battery_identification_trust_tier.Description: Controls what battery self-identification does with its estimate. 'observe' (default) writes the estimate to a JSON file and the log only. 'suggest' additionally publishes two read-only Home Assistant sensors (identified capacity and round-trip efficiency) and logs a recommendation. Neither tier changes the configured battery values used by the optimizer. Defaults to 'observe'.

battery_identification_model_max_age.Description: Maximum age in hours before the battery identification estimate is re-fitted from fresh Home Assistant history. If the saved result is older than this value, a new estimate is produced. Set to 0 to force re-fitting on every call. Defaults to 24 hours (1 day).

pv_module_model.Description: The PV module model. Enter the exact CEC database name, or enter the nominal power in Watts (e.g., 300) to automatically use the closest matching panel. Can be a list for mixed orientation systems.

pv_inverter_model.Description: The PV inverter model. Enter the exact CEC database name, or enter the nominal AC power in Watts (e.g., 5000) to automatically use the closest matching inverter. Can be a list for mixed orientation systems.

surface_tilt.Description: The tilt angle of your solar panels. Defaults to 30. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

surface_azimuth.Description: The azimuth of your PV installation. Defaults to 205. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

modules_per_string.Description: The number of modules per string. Defaults to 16. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

strings_per_inverter.Description: The number of used strings per inverter. Defaults to 1. This parameter can be a list of items to enable the simulation of mixed orientation systems.

number_of_deferrable_loads.Description: Define the number of deferrable loads (appliances to shift) to consider. Defaults to 1 - add more with the load tabs below as needed.

load_names.Description: Name per load tab (for example: Washing Machine, Dishwasher, Pool Pump).

load_type.Description: Select the control profile per load: program-based cycle (washer/dryer/dishwasher), fixed power splittable over time (e-bike charging), fixed power non-splittable block, or variable power and variable time.

load_washdata_enabled.Description: Only relevant for the 'program_based' load type above. Enable to link this load to a real appliance tracked by the WashData 'ha_washdata' custom integration, revealing the device picker below instead of hand-typing programs/power values.

load_washdata_device.Description: Only shown when 'Use a WashData device' above is enabled. Pick the appliance tracked by the WashData 'ha_washdata' custom integration (matching its sensor.<device>_profiel_<program>_aantal / binary_sensor.<device>_actief entities). EMHASS discovers every learned program for that device fresh each optimization cycle (unlike most other per-load fields, this is never frozen at config-save time), and uses the most-used program's learned power_profile/power_profile_interval_min - and its implied duration - instead of this load's flat nominal_power_of_deferrable_loads/operating_hours_of_each_deferrable_load. See 'Program select sensor' below to pin a specific program instead of the most-used one. Falls back gracefully to the flat model if no learned program is found yet.

manual_load_enabled.Description: Master switch for the manually-committed load behaviour below. Enables appliances that have no smart-plug control (e.g. a washing machine or dishwasher with only a physical delay-start timer) to be marked manual per-load via 'Manually-committed load'. When a manual load's ready sensor is turned on, EMHASS computes an optimal start time once and publishes it as an instruction - that commitment is then pinned and will not move on later re-optimizations, since the user has already physically set the appliance's timer.

is_manual_load.Description: One per deferrable load. Enable to treat this load as manually-committed: EMHASS uses this load's own name/nominal power/operating hours (or its resolved WashData profile, if 'Use a WashData device' above is enabled) together with the ready/confirmation/program-select sensors below, instead of scheduling it automatically like a normal deferrable load. Requires 'Enable manually-committed loads' to be on.

manual_load_ready_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. The Home Assistant entity ID of an input_boolean (or similar) that the user turns on to signal they want this load to run. EMHASS reads this each optimization cycle to decide whether to commit a start time for that load.

manual_load_program_select_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load and 'WashData device' above resolved more than one learned program. The Home Assistant entity ID of a select you set to the program you're about to run (e.g. select.wasmachine_cyclusprogramma, an entity WashData already provides). EMHASS matches its current option against the discovered programs and pins the plan to that exact one; without it, or while it's left on "auto_detect", EMHASS falls back to the most-used discovered program.

manual_load_deadline_hour.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. Optional latest time of day this load must be finished by. Leave empty to allow scheduling anywhere in the optimization horizon.

manual_load_confirm_power_sensor.Description: One per deferrable load - only used when 'Manually-committed load' is enabled for that load. Optional Home Assistant entity ID of a power sensor (e.g. a smart plug that can measure but not safely switch the appliance). When set, EMHASS uses it only to detect that the appliance has actually started, to automatically clear the commitment - never to control the appliance.

load_dispatch_mode.Description: Per-load optimization mode: hours (runtime via operating hours) or energy_kwh (deliver target energy). Program-based sequencing is controlled by the load type itself.

load_programs.Description: For program_based loads: JSON list of programs. Each program has name and power_pattern (comma-separated watts per step).

required_energy_kwh_of_each_deferrable_l.Description: Used when dispatch mode is energy_kwh. Defines energy that must be delivered during the optimization horizon.

nominal_power_of_deferrable_loads.Description: The nominal (calculated max) power for each deferrable load in Watts.

minimum_power_of_deferrable_loads.Description: The minimum power for each deferrable load in Watts.

cost_forecast_per_deferrable_load.Description: Optional per-deferrable-load cost forecast track (Currency/kWh) that overrides the shared load_cost_forecast for that specific load - works for any deferrable load, not just heating. Useful whenever one load is priced differently than the rest, e.g. a gas boiler on a gas tariff while an EV charger or heat pump is priced on electricity, or a load with its own dynamic contract. Pass null/None for any load that should keep the shared tariff. Runtime parameter - not cached.

operating_hours_of_each_deferrable_load.Description: The total number of hours that each deferrable load should operate. Fractional values are accepted (e.g. 4.5) and scheduled as the exact nominal_power * hours of energy; for control finer than the optimization timestep use operating_timesteps_of_each_deferrable_load.

treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont.Description: When configuring a deferrable load, set treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont = True if the device should only switch fully on or off (for example, a basic hot water heater), or set treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont = False if the device supports variable power control within its range (for example, an EV charger with adjustable charging rate).

set_deferrable_load_single_constant.friendly_name: Deferrable load run single constant per optimization
set_deferrable_load_single_constant.Description: Define if we should set each deferrable load as a constant fixed value variable with just one startup for each optimization task

set_deferrable_startup_penalty.Description: For penalty P, each time the deferrable load turns on will incur an additional cost of nominal_power (kW) * cost_of_electricity * time step at that time

deferrable_load_max_cost.Description: Maximum acceptable cost for scheduling each deferrable load. If the cost to schedule the load (including startup penalty) exceeds this threshold, the load will not be scheduled. Set to 0 to disable and make load scheduling mandatory.

set_deferrable_max_startups.Description: Set the maximum number of times each deferrable load can be turned on during the optimization horizon. Set to 0 to disable this limit.

def_minimum_on_time.Description: Per-load minimum number of consecutive optimization timesteps a load must stay ON once started (min-up-time / short-cycle protection). One integer per deferrable load. Set to 0 (default) to disable for that load -- default-off, exact no-op. 1 timestep = optimization_time_step minutes (e.g. 3 timesteps at 30-min resolution = 90 minutes minimum run). Intended primarily for treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont loads (heat pumps, AC, pumps) where the ON/OFF binary is tightly coupled to the full nominal power. For plain/continuous-power loads the constraint holds the binary state ON but the power level may be fractional. Composes cleanly with set_deferrable_max_startups (independent constraints). Note: when the minimum ON window cannot fit within the load's operating-window end, the solver simply does not start the load for that horizon rather than forcing infeasibility.

def_minimum_off_time.Description: Per-load minimum number of consecutive optimization timesteps a load must stay OFF once it stops (min-down-time / short-cycle protection). One integer per deferrable load. Set to 0 (default) to disable for that load -- default-off, exact no-op. 1 timestep = optimization_time_step minutes (e.g. 3 timesteps at 30-min resolution = 90 minutes minimum off-time). Intended primarily for treat_deferrable_load_as_semi_cont loads (heat pumps, AC, compressors) where rapid ON-OFF-ON cycling causes wear or violates manufacturer limits. Composes cleanly with def_minimum_on_time and set_deferrable_max_startups (independent constraints). Note: when the minimum OFF window cannot fit within the remaining horizon, the solver simply defers the next start; the problem stays Optimal. Excludes single-constant and sequence loads (same gating as def_minimum_on_time).

set_use_battery.Description: Set to True if we should consider an energy storage device such as a Li-Ion battery. Defaults to False

number_of_batteries.Description: Define the number of physical batteries in the plant. Defaults to 1. When greater than 1, every per-battery array parameter below (capacity, power limits, efficiencies, SOC min/max/target, stress cost, weight_battery_charge/discharge, SOC deficit/surplus threshold/cost) accepts either a single scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly this many entries. See docs/config.md for the full broadcast/nesting semantics.

set_nocharge_from_grid.Description: Set this to true if you want to forbid charging the battery from the grid. The battery will only be charged from excess PV

set_nodischarge_to_grid.friendly_name: Forbid battery discharge to the grid
set_nodischarge_to_grid.Description: Set this to true if you want to forbid discharging battery power to the grid.

set_battery_first_priority.Description: Set this to true to prefer draining stored battery energy before importing from the grid, so the battery is used up before any import while it is still above its minimum SoC. Useful on a flat (non time-of-use) tariff. This is a soft penalty, not a hard constraint: importing while the battery is charged is heavily penalized so drain-first wins on a flat tariff, but the optimizer can still import when that is the only feasible option, so it will not make the problem infeasible.

set_battery_dynamic.Description: Set a power dynamic limiting condition to the battery power. This is an additional constraint on the battery dynamic in power per unit of time (timestep), which allows you to set a percentage of the battery’s nominal full power as the maximum power allowed for (dis)charge.

battery_dynamic_max.friendly_name: Maximum percentage of battery discharge per hour
battery_dynamic_max.Description: The maximum positive (for discharge) allowed power variation (in percentage of battery maximum power) per hour. The solver will automatically scale this limit down based on your chosen timestep duration.

battery_dynamic_min.friendly_name: Maximum percentage of battery charge per hour
battery_dynamic_min.Description: The maximum negative (for charge) allowed power variation (in percentage of battery maximum power) per hour. The solver will automatically scale this limit down based on your chosen timestep duration.

weight_battery_discharge.friendly_name: Add cost weight for battery discharge
weight_battery_discharge.Description: An additional weight (currency/ kWh) applied in the cost function to battery usage for discharging. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast) or a list of one entry per battery, each entry itself a scalar or a time series - see docs/config.md for the nesting rules.

weight_battery_charge.friendly_name: Add cost weight for battery charge
weight_battery_charge.Description: An additional weight (currency/ kWh) applied in the cost function to battery usage for charging. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast) or a list of one entry per battery, each entry itself a scalar or a time series - see docs/config.md for the nesting rules.

battery_discharge_power_max.Description: The maximum discharge power in Watts. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_charge_power_max.Description: The maximum charge power in Watts. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_discharge_efficiency.Description: The discharge efficiency. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_charge_efficiency.Description: The charge efficiency. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_nominal_energy_capacity.Description: The total capacity of the battery stack in Wh. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_minimum_state_of_charge.Description: The minimum allowable battery state of charge. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_maximum_state_of_charge.Description: The maximum allowable battery state of charge. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_target_state_of_charge.Description: The desired battery state of charge at the end of each optimization cycle. (percentage/100). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries; also the per-battery fallback target used by the soc_init/soc_final runtime chain.

battery_stress_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh) applied at the battery's nominal power to penalise high loads. Currently implemented as a quadratic curve (Cost ∝ Power²), incentivising 'low and slow' operation to reduce thermal stress and smooth power flows. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_stress_segments.Description: The number of linear segments used to approximate the stress cost curve. Higher values increase accuracy but may slightly increase computation time.

battery_soc_deficit_threshold.Description: The SOC threshold below which deficit penalties apply. For example, 0.20 for 20% SOC. Penalties are applied for every hour and every kWh the SOC is below this value. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_deficit_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh/h) applied for each kWh of SOC deficit per hour. This penalizes periods when the battery SOC falls below the deficit threshold. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_surplus_threshold.Description: The SOC threshold above which surplus penalties apply. For example, 0.90 for 90% SOC. Penalties are applied for every hour and every kWh the SOC is above this value. Use together with battery_soc_surplus_cost to discourage long dwell near full charge. With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

battery_soc_surplus_cost.Description: A virtual cost (Currency/kWh/h) applied for each kWh of SOC above the surplus threshold per hour. This penalizes periods when the battery SOC sits above the surplus threshold, delaying charging into expected solar peaks and reducing time spent near full charge (battery longevity). Defaults to 0.0 (disabled). With number_of_batteries > 1, accepts a scalar (broadcast to every battery) or a list of exactly number_of_batteries entries.

capacity_cost_per_kw.Description: A cost (currency per kW) applied to the peak grid import power over the optimisation horizon, for tariffs with a capacity or demand charge. 0 (default) disables it and leaves the plan unchanged. A positive value makes the optimiser flatten the import peak, trading it off against energy cost in a single pass. The peak is priced once (it is a power charge, not energy), so set it to the marginal value of shaving 1 kW of peak.

ignore_pv_feedback_during_curtailment.Description: When set to true, prevents PV forecast from being updated with real PV data, avoiding flip-flop behavior during curtailment operations

set_use_heatpump.Description: Set to true to enable heat pump optimization and thermal comfort scheduling.

heatpump_config_mode.Description: room_list: configure heating per room below (Rooms section), each using the model chosen in 'Thermal model family'. graph_topology: ignore the room list entirely and instead configure the whole heating system as a graph (Heat topology below) - lets you express hybrid setups (e.g. gas + heat pump feeding the same buffer) that a flat room list can't. Most single-heat-pump setups want room_list.

heat_topology.Description: Only used when 'Configuration mode' above is graph_topology. Declarative directed graph of heat sources, thermal storage, consumers, and flows. When set, EMHASS compiles this into the flat optim_conf primitives (def_load_config, shared_thermal_tanks, deferrable_load_groups, cost_forecast_per_deferrable_load) automatically. Lets you express hybrid heating setups (gas + heat pump feeding the same DHW + buffer) without hand-rolling the deferrable-load indices. See docs/heat_topology.md for the schema.

is_electric_load.Description: Only used when 'Configuration mode' above is graph_topology. Per-deferrable-load boolean. True (default) means the load draws from the electric balance (heat pumps, electric heaters). False means the load consumes a non-electric commodity (gas, oil, district heating) and contributes only to its thermal target, not to the electric power balance. Auto-populated by the heat_topology compiler based on source type but can be overridden directly.

heatpump_model_family.Description: Per-room demand model used in room_list mode: simple (thermal-loss-only, the long-standing default), physics (real envelope/RC-network demand model using the per-room fields on the Rooms tab), machine_learning/deep_learning (selectable now, currently behave like simple - live dispatch integration for the two-stage/PINN models is a separate, future change).

heatpump_dl_model_name.Description: Placeholder for future deep-learning model selection.

heatpump_use_pinn.Description: Enable Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) based thermal forecasting.

heatpump_pinn_auto_train.Description: Automatically train the PINN model using historical data. No model path is required.

heatpump_pinn_lookahead.Description: Number of 15-minute steps forecast by the PINN model. Default is 144 (36 hours).

heatpump_ml_model_name.Description: Placeholder for future machine-learning model selection.

heatpump_ml_model_path.Description: Placeholder for future machine-learning model path.

heatpump_two_stage_data_csv.Description: CSV path used by the thermal two-stage planner (runtime history + weather/features). Relative paths are resolved from EMHASS root.

heatpump_two_stage_model_dir.Description: Directory containing classical thermal models and metadata for the two-stage planner.

heatpump_two_stage_horizon.Description: Planning horizon in timesteps used by coarse/fine two-stage evaluation.

heatpump_two_stage_top_k.Description: Number of best coarse models to pass to fine-stage selection.

heatpump_two_stage_coarse_models.Description: Optional model names (comma-separated per entry) to limit coarse-stage evaluation. Leave empty to auto-discover.

heatpump_two_stage_fine_models.Description: Optional model names (comma-separated per entry) to limit fine-stage evaluation. Leave empty to auto-discover.

heatpump_nominal_power.Description: Maximum electrical input power of the heat pump in watts. Used for the shared-power-group cap, independent of the model family selected below.

heatpump_is_hybrid.Description: Enable if the system is hybrid (electric heat pump + gas boiler).

hybrid_heatpump_refit_enabled.friendly_name: Enable heat pump electric/gas model auto-refit
hybrid_heatpump_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit a physics-informed model of this heat pump's electric power draw (and gas consumption, if heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured) from weather/duty/history, against fresh Home Assistant history (hybrid-heatpump-model-refit action), and deploy it for hybrid-heatpump-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb, and heatpump_indoor_temp_sensor/heatpump_power_sensor/heatpump_duty_sensor to be configured (used as fit targets/inputs, not optional). Works for a pure-electric heat pump too - just leave heatpump_gas_meter_sensor empty and the gas part is skipped entirely.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each heat pump electric/gas model refit.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_max_electric_mae_w.Description: A refit is only deployed if its electric-power fit MAE (this field) - and, when a gas sensor is configured, its gas-consumption fit MAE too - is under the threshold(s), measured on a held-out slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

hybrid_heatpump_refit_max_gas_mae_m3.Description: Only used when heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured (ignored for a pure-electric refit). A refit is only deployed if BOTH its gas-consumption fit MAE (this field) and its electric-power fit MAE are under their thresholds, measured on a held-out slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

hybrid_heatpump_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward electric-power forecast (and gas-consumption forecast, if the deployed model was fit with a gas sensor configured) using the fitted model (hybrid-heatpump-forecast action). Requires a deployed model (run hybrid-heatpump-model-refit at least once). Holds the last observed heat pump duty constant across the forecast horizon - a known simplification, not a claim of a planned dispatch schedule.

self_learning_physics_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit an online-adaptive (RLS) multi-room model of electric power, gas consumption (if a gas sensor is configured), and every configured room's own temperature, against fresh Home Assistant history (self-learning-physics-refit action), and deploy it for self-learning-physics-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb, heatpump_power_sensor and heatpump_duty_sensor, plus at least one room with heatpump_room_temp_sensors configured. Rooms declared as coupled_neighbors of each other let the model learn a thermal coupling coefficient between them from history, in addition to the manually-entered heatpump_room_coupling_conductance - see self_learning_physics_coupling_source for how the two relate.

self_learning_physics_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each self-learning-physics model refit.

self_learning_physics_forgetting_factor.Description: Recursive-least-squares forgetting factor (0-1]. Lower values adapt faster to recent data but are noisier; 1.0 is a plain (non-forgetting) fit that weighs the whole refit window equally.

self_learning_physics_ridge.Description: Initial RLS regularisation strength. Larger values start the fit more conservatively (slower initial adaptation, more resistant to noise); smaller values adapt faster but can overreact to a noisy start.

self_learning_physics_refit_max_electric.Description: A refit is only deployed if its electric-power fit MAE (this field), its gas-consumption fit MAE (when a gas sensor is configured), and every room's own temperature fit MAE are all under their thresholds, measured on a held-out chronological slice of the refit window. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous model is left in place.

self_learning_physics_refit_max_gas_mae_.Description: Only used when heatpump_gas_meter_sensor is configured (ignored for a pure-electric refit). Same held-out acceptance gate as the electric threshold above, for the gas-consumption fit.

self_learning_physics_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward electric-power forecast (and gas-consumption forecast, if the deployed model has one) plus every configured room's own temperature forecast, using the fitted model (self-learning-physics-forecast action). Requires a deployed model (run self-learning-physics-refit at least once). Heat pump duty is resolved from the latest solved dispatch plan when one exists (a real, multi-room-aware trajectory), else the last observed heatpump_duty_sensor value held constant.

self_learning_physics_coupling_enabled.Description: When on (default), rooms declared as heatpump_room_coupled_neighbors of each other get an extra feature in the self-learning-physics fit so the model can learn a thermal coupling coefficient between them, in addition to their own temperature dynamics. When off, every room is fit independently (degrades gracefully to single-zone behaviour) - useful for a single-room install, or to rule out the coupling features while diagnosing a fit.

self_learning_physics_coupling_source.Description: 'informational' (default): the learned per-pair coupling coefficient is only published/logged, so you can compare it against your own manually-entered heatpump_room_coupling_conductance - the manual value keeps driving real dispatch decisions unchanged. 'auto_dispatch': for any pair the learned model actually covers, its fitted coefficient overrides the manual value used by the live optimizer (heatpump_room_coupling_conductance stays as the fallback for any pair the learned model doesn't cover). Only switch to auto_dispatch once you've compared the two and trust the learned value - a room pair held at a near-constant temperature difference can produce an unreliable learned coefficient regardless of how much history is used.

self_learning_physics_dispatch_max_cache.Description: Only relevant when at least one room has 'Self-learning only' enabled and a fitted model. Driving dispatch directly from the fitted model requires a two-pass solve (a reference pass, then the real solve) because two of its fitted terms are non-linear products of duty and temperature that must first be evaluated against a known temperature trajectory. Re-using the previous solve's own trajectory as that reference (instead of re-running the reference pass every time) is safe for this many consecutive solves, since each room's starting temperature is re-pinned to its real sensor reading every solve regardless. Set to 0 or 1 to always run a fresh reference pass (slower, never stale).

self_learning_physics_opening_relabel_en.Description: Opt-in (default off). At each self-learning-physics-refit, for every room with NEITHER a heatpump_room_window_sensors NOR a heatpump_room_door_sensors entry configured, retroactively infer 'probably open' periods purely from that room's own thermal history (an offline forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass over one-step prediction residuals, repeated self_learning_physics_opening_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into that room's own opening_x_outdoor feature. A room with either sensor configured is never touched by this, for any timestamp, at any iteration - it always uses its real sensor reading instead.

self_learning_physics_opening_relabel_it.Description: Only used when self_learning_physics_opening_relabel_enabled is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop - higher values cost roughly one extra full model fit each, for diminishing returns.

self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_enab.Description: Opt-in (default off). At each self-learning-physics-refit, for every room with NO heatpump_room_blind_sensors entry configured, retroactively infer a continuous (0=open..1=fully closed) blind/shading-position curve purely from that room's own thermal history on sunny periods (an offline forward-filter + RTS-smoother pass over one-step prediction residuals, repeated self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_iterations times, each pass refitting on the newly relabeled data) and feed the result back into that room's own blind_x_dni feature. A room with a configured sensor is never touched by this, for any timestamp, at any iteration - it always uses its real sensor reading instead. Blind position is only ever observable when there is sun (dni) to block or not - a room with too little sunny history in the refit window (e.g. heatpump_weather_dni_sensor left unconfigured) is skipped for that refit rather than guessed at.

self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_iter.Description: Only used when self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_enabled is on. How many fit -> smooth-residuals -> relabel -> refit passes to run per refit. A small fixed count, not a convergence-detection loop. One higher than the opening-relabel default by design: the first pass here is a weaker heuristic bootstrap (no fitted blind_x_dni coefficient exists yet), so one extra calibrated pass meaningfully improves on that weaker start.

self_learning_physics_blind_estimate_sou.friendly_name: Live blind-position estimate: informational vs. dispatch
self_learning_physics_blind_estimate_sou.Description: 'informational' (default): the live Kalman-inferred blind-position estimate (see self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_enabled and the 'Blind Position Estimate' sensor per room) is only computed/persisted/published every naive-mpc-optim cycle, so you can compare it against your own knowledge of when blinds were actually closed - it never reaches the optimizer, which keeps using its existing static blind_position fallback for that room. 'auto_dispatch': for a room whose estimate currently clears its own confidence gate (needs several consecutive sunny cycles of consistent evidence after a good self_learning_physics_blind_relabel_enabled refit - a fresh/uncertain estimate is never used), the live estimate overrides the static fallback for that solve. A wrong blind-position guess has no safe direction (unlike pausing heat for a possibly-open window) - only switch to auto_dispatch once you've compared informational readings against reality and trust them. A room's real heatpump_room_blind_sensors reading, when configured, always takes precedence over any estimate regardless of this setting.

self_learning_physics_opening_confirm_en.Description: Opt-in (default off). Requires self_learning_physics_opening_relabel_enabled to actually be useful. For each room with neither a window nor a door sensor configured, once its EM relabeling has surfaced a candidate opening event, publish a question sensor (sensor.room_opening_confirmation_<room>) asking whether that event really was an open window/door - pair a Home Assistant automation (see docs/automations.md) with 'Room opening confirmation: ready/answer input_boolean' (above) to let you answer from a notification. A confirmed answer becomes permanent ground truth: it's never re-inferred or overwritten by any later refit.

heatpump_can_cool.Description: Enable if the heat pump supports both heating and cooling.

heatpump_indoor_temp_sensor.Description: Optional, and unrelated to 'Thermal model family'/room_list dispatch above - this is a single whole-house sensor used only by two optional whole-house features: (1) the 'Whole-house dispatch' fields directly below, if you've also set a dispatch on/off entity there, and (2) the heating-need forecast's physics model fit (heating-model-refit action), if that's enabled. Per-room dispatch always uses the room temperature sensors on the Rooms tab instead - leave this empty if you don't use either whole-house feature.

heatpump_dispatch_control_entity.friendly_name: Whole-house heat pump on/off entity (HA entity)
heatpump_dispatch_control_entity.Description: Home Assistant switch entity_id for the whole-house heat pump's on/off control. EMHASS never calls this entity's service directly - it only publishes a dispatch target sensor for a companion HA automation to apply.

heatpump_dispatch_min_temperature.Description: Minimum indoor temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_max_temperature.Description: Maximum indoor temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_target_temperature.Description: Fallback target indoor temperature for the whole-house heat pump dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_nominal_power.Description: Nominal heating power of the whole-house heat pump, used by the thermal_battery model for the dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_supply_temperature.Description: Heating supply/flow temperature used to estimate the heat pump COP for the dispatch load.

heatpump_dispatch_volume.Description: Effective volume used by the thermal_battery model to convert heat input into a temperature change for the dispatch load.

heatpump_weather_ghi_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for global horizontal irradiance (GHI).

heatpump_weather_dni_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for direct normal irradiance (DNI).

heatpump_weather_dhi_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI).

heatpump_weather_wind_speed_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for wind speed.

heatpump_weather_wind_direction_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for wind direction.

heatpump_weather_humidity_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for relative humidity.

heatpump_power_sensor.friendly_name: Heat pump electric power sensor (HA entity)
heatpump_power_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for real-time heat pump electrical power in watts. A cumulative kWh energy meter also works - refits automatically detect a cumulative reading (values that only ever rise) and convert it to an average power in W (assuming the meter's cumulative unit is kWh) before fitting. Also used live during naive-mpc-optim (together with the duty sensor below) by the sensorless window/door-open Kalman detector, to know how much heat was actually delivered since the last dispatch cycle.

heatpump_flow_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for measured heating circuit flow temperature in °C.

heatpump_gas_meter_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for gas usage when hybrid operation is enabled. Either a raw cumulative meter totalizer (the usual state_class=total_increasing HA convention) or an already-incremental consumption-per-interval sensor works - refits automatically detect a cumulative reading (values that only ever rise) and convert it to a per-interval delta before fitting.

heatpump_outdoor_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for measured outdoor temperature history, used to fit/refit the thermal-mass physics model (heating-model-refit action).

heatpump_duty_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the heat pump's measured on/off or duty-cycle state history, used to fit/refit the thermal-mass physics model (heating-model-refit action). Also used live during naive-mpc-optim by the sensorless window/door-open Kalman detector - see 'Heat pump electric power sensor' above.

heatpump_control_mode.Description: Choose how the optimizer sets thermal control: weather_curve, thermostat_sensor, or direct_setpoint.

heatpump_target_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant entity_id for the target thermostat temperature. Visible only when control strategy is 'thermostat_sensor'.

heatpump_curve_intercept.Description: Weather-curve intercept: flow_temp = slope × outdoor_temp + intercept. Default is 40.0.

heatpump_curve_slope.Description: Weather-curve slope. Typically negative (e.g. -1.0): colder outdoor temperature leads to higher flow temperature.

heatpump_max_deviation.Description: Maximum allowed deviation from the weather curve flow temperature.

heatpump_supply_temp_min.Description: Absolute minimum flow temperature allowed for heat pump operation.

heatpump_supply_temp_max.Description: Absolute maximum flow temperature allowed for heat pump operation.

heating_forecast_enabled.Description: Publish a forward indoor-temperature forecast (heating assumed off) and a 'heating needed by' sensor, using the fitted thermal-mass physics model. Requires data/thermal_physics_params.json to exist (fit it once with scripts/thermal_mass_physics_model.py).

heating_forecast_horizon_hours.Description: How far forward to simulate the indoor temperature. Requesting a horizon longer than the weather forecast actually returned (controlled by delta_forecast_daily on the triggering call) is logged as a mismatch rather than failing.

heating_forecast_comfort_min_temp.Description: Indoor temperature below which 'heating needed by' fires. Compared against the forecast after the safety margin below is subtracted.

heating_forecast_safety_margin_c.Description: Defensive offset subtracted from the simulated temperature before the comfort-floor check, so the warning fires earlier rather than later. The physics model has a confirmed tendency to run warm in open-loop simulation.

heating_model_refit_enabled.Description: Periodically refit the thermal-mass physics model's parameters against fresh Home Assistant history (heating-model-refit action) and deploy them for heating-need-forecast to use. Requires use_influxdb (see docs/passing_data.md) since the refit window is longer than Home Assistant's own recorder retention.

heating_model_refit_window_days.Description: How many days of history to retrieve for each refit.

heating_model_refit_max_mae_c.Description: A refit is only deployed (overwrites the previous fitted parameters) if its room-temperature fit MAE is under this value. A worse fit is logged as an error and the previous parameters are left in place, protecting against deploying a fit from e.g. a sensor outage during the refit window.

heatpump_number_of_rooms.Description: Number of controlled rooms. This defines how many room tabs and room-level sensor entries are used.

heatpump_room_names.Description: List of room names used for room sub-tab labels. Keep the same order as room sensor arrays.

heatpump_room_self_learning_only.Description: When a fitted self-learning-physics model exists for this room AND that fit is actually more accurate than the physics/simple model would have been for the same room over the same history (self-learning-physics-refit checks this automatically, per room - not a fixed threshold), this room's dispatch is driven directly by that model's own fitted equation instead of the physics/simple thermal_battery model - 'Room supply temperature' and any physics envelope fields for this room become informational only. Falls back to the physics/simple model, with a log message explaining why, whenever no fitted model exists yet OR the fitted model isn't actually an improvement for this room - never crashes. Also see 'Self-learning dispatch: reference-solve cache age' below.

heatpump_room_temp_sensors.Description: Home Assistant temperature sensor entity_ids per room. For multiple sensors in one room, enter a comma-separated list (e.g. sensor.room1_temp_1,sensor.room1_temp_2). Keep room order aligned with room names.

heatpump_room_valve_sensors.friendly_name: Room TRV valve position sensors (HA entities, optional)
heatpump_room_valve_sensors.Description: Optional HA sensor entity_ids for thermostatic valve position per room. For multiple sensors in one room, enter a comma-separated list. Expected value range is 0 to 1 (0=closed, 1=open).

heatpump_room_valve_mode.Description: Whether this room's TRV (above) is modulating (continuously variable position, e.g. 0-1) or on/off (binary open/closed, only ever reports 0 or 1). Currently informational/documentation only - it isn't yet read by any dispatch logic - but it's picked up as a feature by the ML/two-stage thermal model, and prevents misreading an on/off valve's 0-or-1 readings as a smooth modulating signal.

heatpump_room_blind_sensors.Description: Optional HA sensor entity_ids for blind or shading position per room. For multiple sensors in one room, enter a comma-separated list. Expected value range is 0 to 1 (0=open/no shading, 1=fully closed/max shading) - a raw Home Assistant 'cover' entity's native current_position is usually the OPPOSITE polarity and a 0-100 scale, so pointing this directly at a cover entity will likely need an inverting/normalizing template sensor first (this field is not auto-detected or rescaled). Now actually used: reduces direct solar gain for a 'physics' family room with 'Room blind/shading type' set (below), and feeds the self-learning-physics model's own learned blind-effectiveness feature for a self-learning room - both leave shading at 0 (no effect) when this sensor is left unset.

heatpump_room_blind_type.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics AND 'Room blind/shading sensors' (above) is configured for this room. Physics model for how this room's shading reduces solar gain - applied to the DIRECT solar component only (diffuse gain, from the whole sky dome, is never blocked by either type). 'screen' = a blind sitting flush on the window glass, blocks a fraction of direct sun equal to its own position regardless of the sun's angle. 'awning' (e.g. a knikarmscherm) = projects outward above the window, only blocks direct sun once the sun is high enough in the sky - little to no effect in early morning, late evening, or winter. 'none' (default) disables shading entirely. A self-learning-physics room ignores this field completely - it learns its own blind's real effectiveness directly from data instead (see 'Self-learning dispatch' further down).

heatpump_room_window_sensors.Description: Optional HA binary_sensor entity_id for this room's window open/closed state (one entity per room). Now actually used: while reported open, this room's heating is paused and an extra ventilation-loss term is added for the current dispatch step (physics family), or the self-learning-physics model's own learned opening-loss feature picks it up (self-learning room) - both are inert (no effect) when left unset. A live 'window is open' signal can't be forecast, so this only ever affects the current/near-term step, never future ones. Leaving this unset does NOT disable detection entirely: a per-room Kalman filter always runs alongside it, inferring 'probably open' purely from the room's own thermal behaviour (predicted vs. observed temperature) - a real sensor here is never overridden, only ever agreed with or supplemented.

heatpump_room_door_sensors.Description: Optional HA binary_sensor entity_id for this room's door open/closed state (one entity per room). Now actually used: gets the exact same pause-heating/extra-ventilation-loss treatment as 'Room window sensors' above, PLUS - while open - boosts this room's thermal coupling to any declared neighbor room(s) ('Coupled neighbor rooms'/self-learning's own learned coupling); simply has no coupling effect when no neighbors are declared. Both effects are inert when left unset. Same current-step-only limitation as the window sensor above. The always-on Kalman fallback described there also applies here for the pause/ventilation-loss effect (never for the neighbor-coupling boost, which stays sensor-only) - see 'Room window sensors' above.

heatpump_room_opening_confirm_ready_sens.friendly_name: Room opening confirmation: ready input_boolean (HA entity, optional)
heatpump_room_opening_confirm_ready_sens.Description: Only used when 'Enable retroactive opening-open relabeling' AND 'Enable opening-confirmation questions' are both on, and this room has NEITHER a window NOR a door sensor configured above. A per-room Home Assistant input_boolean you flip to 'on' once you've set 'Room opening confirmation: answer input_boolean' (below) to your answer - the paired sensor.room_opening_confirmation_<room> question sensor explains exactly what's being asked and when. Mirrors the mechanism of the existing manual-load ready/confirm sensors, applied to opening confirmations instead.

heatpump_room_opening_confirm_answer_sen.friendly_name: Room opening confirmation: answer input_boolean (HA entity, optional)
heatpump_room_opening_confirm_answer_sen.Description: Only used together with 'Room opening confirmation: ready input_boolean' above. A per-room Home Assistant input_boolean holding your answer to the most recent opening-confirmation question for this room: on = yes, it really was open; off = no, it was closed. Read once the paired ready sensor is set to on.

heatpump_room_min_temperature.Description: Per-room minimum comfort temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint. Keep room order aligned with room names.

heatpump_room_max_temperature.Description: Per-room maximum comfort temperature used as a hard thermal_battery constraint. Keep room order aligned with room names.

heatpump_room_target_temperature.Description: Per-room fallback target temperature, used when no thermal comfort schedule band is configured for a timestep.

heatpump_room_nominal_power.Description: Per-room nominal heating power used by the thermal_battery model for this room's deferrable load.

heatpump_room_supply_temperature.Description: Per-room heating supply/flow temperature used to estimate the heat pump COP for this room's deferrable load.

heatpump_room_volume.Description: Per-room air volume used by the thermal_battery model to convert heat input into a temperature change.

heatpump_room_shared_group.Description: Per-room group id (0 = none) for rooms sharing one physical heat pump. Rooms with the same non-zero group id jointly cannot exceed 'heatpump_nominal_power'.

heatpump_room_coupled_neighbors.Description: Per-room comma-separated list of 0-based room indices this room exchanges heat with through a shared wall/floor (e.g. '0,2'). Positionally aligned with 'Coupling conductance' below - the first conductance entry applies to the first neighbor index, etc. Leave empty for no coupling. Independent of 'Room shared heat pump group' above - that caps shared electrical power, this models actual heat flow between rooms and affects real dispatch decisions.

heatpump_room_coupling_conductance.Description: Per-room comma-separated list of wall/floor conductance values (kW per °C of temperature difference), one per entry in 'Coupled neighbor rooms' above, same order. Higher means more heat crosses per degree of difference between the two rooms.

heatpump_room_u_value.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room overall heat-transfer coefficient of the building envelope - higher means more heat loss per degree of indoor/outdoor difference.

heatpump_room_envelope_area.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room total external surface area (walls/roof/floor exposed to outside) the U-value applies to. Must be non-zero for the physics model to produce any heat-loss demand.

heatpump_room_ventilation_rate.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room air changes per hour, used to estimate ventilation heat loss.

heatpump_room_window_area.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room total window area used for solar gain estimation. Set to 0 to disable solar gain contribution for that room.

heatpump_room_shgc.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room window solar heat gain coefficient (0-1). Typical double glazing range: 0.4-0.6.

heatpump_room_internal_gains_factor.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room constant internal heat gains from occupants and appliances.

heatpump_room_thermal_inertia_time_const.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room time constant (hours) describing how fast the room cools when the heat pump is off. Higher values indicate better insulation/more thermal mass.

heatpump_room_carnot_efficiency.Description: Only used when 'Thermal model family' (Heat Pump tab) is physics. Per-room fraction of the theoretical Carnot COP the heat pump actually achieves - used together with supply/outdoor temperature to compute a real per-timestep COP, replacing a single fixed nominal COP.

set_use_boiler.Description: Enable boiler or thermal tank optimization.

number_of_boilers.Description: Number of DHW storage systems to optimize.

boiler_names.Description: Boiler labels for diagnostics and logs.

boiler_type.Description: resistive (flat COP=1.0), hpboiler (standalone heat-pump water heater, its own fixed carnot_efficiency), or hp_tank_zone (DHW heated through the same physical unit as a space-heating load - set 'Coupled space-heating load index' below to have it use that load's actual carnot_efficiency instead of its own, since it's the same real-world equipment).

boiler_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant sensor entity_id for current boiler water temperature.

boiler_target_temp_sensor.Description: Home Assistant sensor entity_id for boiler target temperature.

boiler_volume_l.Description: Water volume per boiler in liters.

boiler_supply_temperature.Description: Supply temperature used to estimate COP for heat-pump based boiler types.

boiler_start_temperature.Description: Initial tank temperature at optimization start.

boiler_power_sensor.Description: Home Assistant sensor entity_id for current boiler electrical power in watts.

boiler_min_temperature.Description: Lower bound for boiler water temperature.

boiler_loss_factor.Description: Thermal loss factor per timestep for the tank model.

boiler_dhw_draw_kwh_forecast.Description: CSV or JSON list per boiler defining hot-water draw profile in kWh per timestep.

boiler_legionella_hold_hours.Description: Minimum duration to stay above legionella target temperature.

boiler_legionella_last_run_iso.Description: Last successful anti-legionella timestamp in ISO-8601 format.

boiler_legionella_force_resistive.Description: When true, forces resistive behavior on due legionella cycles even for HP-based boiler types.

boiler_coupled_heatpump_load_index.Description: For hp_tank_zone: index of the coupled space-heating deferrable load (e.g. a room or the whole-house heat pump dispatch load). -1 disables coupling. When set, the boiler's COP is computed from that load's own carnot_efficiency instead of a flat placeholder - same physical heat pump, so the same real-world efficiency factor applies - while the boiler keeps its own (typically higher) DHW supply temperature.

boiler_hp_shared_max_power.Description: For hp_tank_zone: shared electrical power cap for boiler + coupled heatpump load.

boiler_uncertainty_margin_kwh.Description: Phase-3 hedge margin added to comfort reserves against DHW uncertainty.

boiler_max_temperature.Description: Upper bound for boiler water temperature.

set_use_ev_charger.Description: Enable EV charging settings in the configuration UI.

number_of_ev_chargers.Description: Number of EV charge points to configure.

ev_charger_names.Description: Name for each EV charge point tab.

ev_charge_mode_service.Description: Home Assistant select entity_id used to set charger mode (for example: select.charge_mode or select.myenergi_zappi_charge_mode).

ev_phase_select_entity.Description: Home Assistant select entity_id used to switch charger phase mode when auto 1/3 phase is enabled (for example: select.phase_selection or select.myenergi_zappi_phase_setting).

ev_charge_mode_stopped_value.Description: Required value sent to the charger integration for Stopped mode.

ev_charge_mode_fast_value.Description: Optional value sent to the charger integration for Fast mode.

ev_charge_mode_eco_value.Description: Optional value sent to the charger integration for Eco mode.

ev_charge_mode_ecoplus_value.Description: Optional value sent to the charger integration for Eco+ mode.

ev_charge_mode_variable_value.Description: Optional value sent to the charger integration for Variable mode.

ev_phase_select_value_1_phase.Description: Value to write to the phase selection select entity for 1-phase charging (for example: 1_phase).

ev_phase_select_value_3_phase.Description: Value to write to the phase selection select entity for 3-phase charging (for example: 3_phase).

ev_phase_select_value_auto.Description: Value to write to the phase selection select entity for automatic phase switching (for example: automatic).
